Resonators.notes: Read from src/Resonators.cpp at commit fb01326, the commit whose plugin.json carries the installed 2.11.1. The manual is written for 2.11.0 and says nothing about this module that the code contradicts. Two things it leaves out. The AMP knob scales only what reaches the OUT jack; the WET jack carries the four resonators at their GAIN settings alone (Resonators.cpp:246 against 250). And the polyphonic CV jacks fall back to their last channel rather than to zero when they carry fewer than four channels (Resonators.cpp:183, 195 and 205), so a monophonic cable into DECAY, COLOR or GAIN moves all four resonators. The COLOR figures come from Resonators.cpp:197 to 234: the knob is turned into a factor of 100 to the power of twice the knob minus one, which multiplies a 20000Hz lowpass and a 20Hz highpass, both clamped to 20Hz and 20000Hz.

TwinPeaks.notes: Read from src/TwinPeaks.cpp and src/filter/ripples.hpp at commit fb01326, the commit whose plugin.json carries the installed 2.11.1. The manual describes FM A and FM B as controlling the total amount of modulation, which is right: ripples.hpp:154 multiplies the whole sum of FM jack, TRACK and XFM-B by that knob before it reaches the cutoff. ripples.hpp:156 then takes the minimum of that sum and zero, so upward modulation past the knob's own 20kHz maximum does nothing; the manual does not mention the cap. The LP-TWP jack is the one input on the module that is read outside the polyphony loop (TwinPeaks.cpp:130), so it is monophonic while everything else follows the audio input's channel count. ripples.hpp:163 adds a microvolt of noise to the input, which is what starts self-oscillation.

Euler.notes: Read from src/Euler.cpp at commit fb01326, the commit whose plugin.json carries the installed 2.11.1. The FREQ knob runs from -8 to 4 and is shown as two to that power in hertz (Euler.cpp:52), so the range is about 0.004Hz to 16Hz with 2Hz at the default. The measurement interval is two divided by that frequency in samples, clamped to between 1 and 1024 (Euler.cpp:85), which the manual does not mention; at the slow end the module measures rarely and the output steps. The 31.5 in the angle formula at Euler.cpp:88 is the scaling that makes a one hertz sine measured at a FREQ of one hertz come out as its cosine, as the manual describes. The module has no context menu of its own.

Rich.notes: Read from src/Rich.cpp at commit fb01326, the commit whose plugin.json carries the installed 2.11.1, alongside docs/Cella_Manual.md, which is written for 2.11.0. The manual's account matches the code. One thing it does not say: the trigger sync window is a delay, not a look-ahead, so Rich.cpp:143 starts the envelope only once the chosen number of samples has passed since the trigger, and the whole envelope is late by that much unless the window is switched off. Bytebeat.notes: Read from src/Bytebeat.cpp at commit fb01326, the commit whose plugin.json carries the installed 2.11.1, alongside docs/Cella_Manual.md written for 2.11.0. The manual calls the second menu item Multiline with an on and off state; the code's item is Submit/New Line with the choices Enter/Shift+Enter and Shift+Enter/Enter (Bytebeat.cpp:437). The three CV knobs are attenuators from 0 to 1 rather than attenuverters (Bytebeat.cpp:127 to 129), so a jack cannot be inverted. The clock rate is measured between rises and clamped to between 0.001Hz and 1000Hz (Bytebeat.cpp:163); the FREQ knob then multiplies half that figure by two to the power of the knob, which is why the hover text changes from hertz to a multiplier when a clock is patched. The expression editor is a LedDisplayTextField, not a parameter, so it has no census position and no click on it can reach a help line.

Bezier.notes: Read from src/Bezier.cpp at commit fb01326, the commit whose plugin.json carries the installed 2.11.1, alongside docs/Cella_Manual.md written for 2.11.0. The manual says the GATE output carries the maximum of zero and the curve; the code puts out a flat 10V or 0V depending on whether the curve is above zero (Bezier.cpp:214), and it tests the curve before the offset is added, so an offset does not move the point at which the gate opens. The manual spells the menu item Asymmetric Curve; the item itself prints Assymetric Curve. The SIGNAL input has no panel label of its own beyond IN and is not described in the manual at all: with a cable in it, the random draw is replaced by whatever voltage is present at that instant. The CLIP, FOLD and WRAP switch positions run top to bottom and the module comes up on CLIP. The Level jack is given no family because it and the FM jack both take plain modulation; the IN jack is given none because it carries whatever is patched.

CognitiveShift.notes: Read from src/CognitiveShift.cpp at commit fb01326, the commit whose plugin.json carries the installed 2.11.1, alongside docs/Cella_Manual.md written for 2.11.0. The manual's account matches the code. Two things it does not spell out. The EDIT button does not merely enable manual entry: CognitiveShift.cpp:269 skips the clock test entirely while it is on, so a running clock is ignored until it is switched off again. And the DAC attenuverters run -1 to 1 rather than 0 to 1 (CognitiveShift.cpp:110 to 113), so a converter output can be inverted. Integral.notes: Read from src/Integral.cpp at commit fb01326, the commit whose plugin.json carries the installed 2.11.1, alongside docs/Cella_Manual.md written for 2.11.0. Two places where the manual and the code differ. The manual says the INIT knob sets a voltage from 0V to 10V; Integral.cpp:154 configures it from -10V to 10V, so it can subtract as well. And the manual gives the gate modes as low meaning 0V and high meaning above 0V, which is right, but the low test is an exact comparison with zero (Integral.cpp:246), so any small offset on the gate counts as high. On the FOLD setting the fold is applied to the output only and the internal total is left alone (Integral.cpp:265 against 260), unlike CLIP and RESET which act on the total itself. The rate figures come from the base time constants of 5s, 0.25s and 0.00125s at Integral.cpp:87 with the knob as a power of two.
